name: answer_back_to_the_agent
title: Tasks · an agent made on call, and the answer to its question goes back to it

steps.say: keep a list of deals: the firm's name and the asking price
steps.reply:
I made a **Deal list** in a new Deals module with two columns: the firm's name and the asking price. It's empty for now. Each firm is also linked to what I know about that company elsewhere.

What currency are the prices in? Tell me and I'll label the column. To add deals, just tell me something like "Acme, 2.5M".
I added Midwest HVAC to your deal list with an asking price of $900,000. It's the first deal on the list.

steps.say: make an agent called Deal Analyst that, when given a task about a deal, works it out from the deal's row, saves what it found on the row with its source, and asks me for anything the row doesn't have
steps.reply:
I've made **Deal Analyst** in your Deals module. It only works when you ask: give it a task or mention it with **@Deal Analyst**, and nothing runs on a schedule.

When you give it a task about a deal, it will:
- **Read the deal's row** in your deal list, plus anything else I know about that firm.
- **Work out the answer** and show which values it used and where each one came from.
- **Save what it found on the same row**, naming the source of each value. Anything it estimates is labelled as an estimate. It won't overwrite a value you entered unless you say so.
- **Ask you on a card** for anyth

steps.say: add a task on Midwest HVAC to ask the broker for 3 years of P&L, give it to the Deal Analyst and start it
steps.reply:
I added "Ask the broker for 3 years of P&L" to Midwest HVAC in your deal list. It's assigned to the Deal Analyst, who should start on it within about half a minute.

Nothing gets sent to the broker without your yes. Any message the Deal Analyst drafts will come to you as a card to approve first. I don't have the broker's name or contact details yet, so if the Deal Analyst can't find them, it will ask you.
